mainTopic: The liquid measuring vessels of the מקדש: how many there were, how they were measured, and what each one was used for
overview: This amud is about the liquid measuring vessels in the מקדש. רבי שמעון holds there was no הין vessel, so he names a one-and-a-half-לוג vessel for the כהן גדול's חביתין as the seventh. He states the rule that each vessel measured only one amount. The גמרא then asks what practical difference comes from רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה listing the vessels in opposite orders. רבי יוחנן ties the order to whether the overflow of the vessels is holy. אביי ties it instead to the meaning of the word מלאים, "full." Next the גמרא explains that the רבנן's הין was the one משה made for the שמן המשחה, and that seven liquid measures is a fixed tradition. A new משנה then lists what each vessel measured, including the oil for מנחות, for animal offerings and for the מנורה. The גמרא opens with רבי's difficulty about why the רביעית vessel needed to be anointed, and this continues on the next amud.

steps.title: רבי שמעון names a one-and-a-half לוג vessel as the seventh measure
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון says the missing seventh vessel was a measure of one and a half לוג, used for the oil of the כהן גדול's daily offering.
steps.simpleTranslation: Which vessel should I put in its place? Rather, there was an extra measuring vessel of one and a half לוג in the מקדש. It was used to measure the oil for the חביתין of the כהן גדול: one and a half לוג in the morning and one and a half לוג in the afternoon.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי שמעון holds there was no הין vessel, so he needs a different vessel to reach seven. He says it was a one-and-a-half-לוג vessel.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The count of seven vessels stays the same, but רבי שמעון swaps out one item on the list. His new vessel matches a real daily need: the כהן גדול's offering used one and a half לוג of oil each morning and each afternoon.

keyTerms.meaning: An additional measuring vessel
A liquid measure (the volume of about six eggs)
The griddle-cake flour offering the כהן גדול brought every day, half in the morning and half in the afternoon
Afternoon (literally 'between the evenings')

phrases.english: Which shall I bring in its place?
Rather, an additional measure
of a log and a half was there,
with which he would measure
for the griddle-cakes of the High Priest –
a log and a half in the morning,
a log and a half in the afternoon.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶת מִי אָבִיא תַּחְתָּיו? אֶלָּא מִדָּה יְתֵירָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues רבי שמעון's statement in the ברייתא, which came before this section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In place of a הין vessel, the מקדש had a one-and-a-half-לוג vessel for the oil of the חביתין of the כהן גדול.

steps.title: The חכמים say a חצי לוג vessel would be enough
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים argue that no special vessel was needed, since the half-לוג vessel could be used three times.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: There was a half-לוג vessel there, and it is possible to measure with the half-לוג vessel.
steps.whatsHappening: The חכמים challenge רבי שמעון's extra vessel. They say the half-לוג vessel, used three times, gives one and a half לוג.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The attack is that the one-and-a-half-לוג vessel is unnecessary. If a smaller vessel already in the מקדש can reach the same amount, there is no reason to make a dedicated vessel for it.

keyTerms.meaning: Half a לוג
To measure or calculate an amount

phrases.aramaic: אָמְרוּ לוֹ: חֲצִי לוֹג הָיְתָה שָׁם,
phrases.english: They said to him: A half-log was there,
and it is possible to measure with the half-log.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרוּ לוֹ: חֲצִי לוֹג הָיְתָה שָׁם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the need for the vessel רבי שמעון proposed in step 1.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי שמעון's claim that a one-and-a-half-לוג vessel existed
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: An amount that a smaller existing vessel can reach by repeated filling does not need its own vessel.

steps.title: רבי שמעון shows their logic proves too much
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון answers that by the חכמים' logic, even the half-לוג and לוג vessels would be unneeded, since a רביעית vessel could measure everything.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: Even according to your words, one should not make a half-לוג or a לוג vessel. There was a רביעית vessel there, and it is possible to measure with the רביעית.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי שמעון turns the חכמים' argument back on them. If smaller vessels can replace larger ones, the half-לוג and לוג vessels on their own list would be pointless too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here he shows that the חכמים' reasoning leads to an absurd result. Everyone agrees there were half-לוג and לוג vessels, so the idea that 'a smaller vessel could do it' cannot be the rule.

keyTerms.meaning: Even according to your own words; turning the other side's logic against them
A quarter of a לוג, the smallest liquid measure on the list

phrases.english: He said to them: Even according to your words,
one should not make a half-log or a log,
a quarter-log was there,
and it is possible to measure with the quarter-log!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the reasoning behind the חכמים' challenge in step 2.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The general idea that a vessel is unnecessary if a smaller one can reach the same amount
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: It proves too much: it would also cancel the half-לוג and לוג vessels, which everyone agrees existed.

steps.title: The rule in the מקדש: one vessel, one measure
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון states the principle that in the מקדש a measuring vessel was used for only one specific amount.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, this was the rule in the מקדש: a vessel used for this measure is not used for a different measure.
steps.whatsHappening: After knocking down the חכמים' logic, רבי שמעון gives the real rule. Each measuring vessel in the מקדש was used for one amount only.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This rule explains why a separate one-and-a-half-לוג vessel was needed. Using the half-לוג vessel three times would mean using it for a different amount than its own, which the מקדש did not do.

keyTerms.meaning: This is the rule
In the Temple
A different measure or amount

steps.whatToRemember: In the מקדש, each measuring vessel served one amount only. So a vessel of one and a half לוג was needed even though smaller vessels existed.

phrases.english: Rather, this was the rule in the Temple:
a vessel that is used for this measure
is not used for a different measure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the positive principle after the rejection in step 3, fully answering the challenge in step 2.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A smaller vessel filled several times could replace a larger dedicated vessel.
steps.terutzMaskana: Each vessel in the מקדש measured only its own amount, so a one-and-a-half-לוג vessel was needed.
steps.whyThisMatters: This rule is the basis for רבי שמעון's list of seven vessels. It explains why the מקדש had a separate vessel for each amount it used.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר ברבי צדוק: the הין had marks
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא closes with רבי אלעזר ברבי צדוק's view that the הין vessel had measuring marks on it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר ברבי צדוק says: There were marks on the הין, and so on.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא ends with a third view, the same one found in the משנה. רבי אלעזר ברבי צדוק says the הין vessel had marks showing different amounts.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In his view, one הין vessel with marked lines could measure several amounts. This is a different picture from רבי שמעון's strict 'one vessel, one measure' rule.

keyTerms.meaning: Marked lines on a vessel showing amounts
A large liquid measure, equal to twelve לוג
And so on; the rest of the quote is left out

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix this up with רבי שמעון's view. רבי שמעון says there was no הין vessel at all. רבי אלעזר ברבי צדוק says there was one, with marks on it.

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar, son of Rabbi Tzadok, says:
There were marks on the hin, etc.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בְּרַבִּי צָדוֹק אוֹמֵר: שְׁנָתוֹת הָיוּ בַּהִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a separate opinion from the ברייתא, which is also found in the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The הין vessel had marked lines showing the amounts needed for the bull, the ram, and the lamb.

steps.title: What is the real difference between the two lists?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what practical difference there is between רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה, who listed the same vessels in a different order.
steps.simpleTranslation: What difference is there between רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why it matters that רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה listed the vessels in different orders. This question sets up the answers that come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both תנאים list the same seven vessels, so it looks like only the order is different. The גמרא assumes that a disagreement must have some real result, so it looks for one.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the difference between, asking for the practical result of a disagreement

phrases.english: What is there between
Rabbi Meir and Rabbi Yehuda?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי אִיכָּא בֵּין רַבִּי מֵאִיר לְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the ברייתא is finished, the גמרא starts analyzing the disagreement in it.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The practical difference that comes from listing the vessels in ascending order or in descending order.

steps.title: They argue about the overflow of the measuring vessels
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says the difference is whether the overflow of a measuring vessel becomes holy.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: The difference between them is the overflow of the measuring vessels.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן gives a short answer: the two תנאים argue about בירוצי מדות, the liquid that spills over the top of a measuring vessel.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When you fill a vessel past its rim, some liquid runs down the outside. רבי יוחנן says the question is whether that extra liquid is made holy by the vessel. The next two steps explain how each order of the list connects to this.

keyTerms.meaning: The overflow of measuring vessels, the liquid that spills down the outside when the vessel is overfilled

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said:
The overflow of the measuring vessels is the difference between them.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: בֵּירוּצֵי מִדּוֹת אִיכָּא בֵּינַיְיהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 6.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The disagreement is about whether the overflow of a measuring vessel becomes holy.

steps.title: Counting upward: the overflow is holy
steps.stepSummary: The one who lists the vessels from small to big holds that the overflow is holy, because משה started with a רביעית and measured upward, so the overflow went in.
steps.simpleTranslation: The one who lists from small to big holds that the overflow of the measures became holy. הקב"ה gave משה a quarter-הין vessel and told him: Measure with it, so the overflow goes in.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן explains the view of the one who lists the vessels from small to big. He says this view holds that the overflow is holy.
steps.deeperAnalysis: משה was given the smallest vessel first and filled bigger vessels by pouring from it. When you pour from a small vessel into a bigger one, the overflow on the outside also goes into the bigger vessel. So the overflow was counted in the original measures, which shows it is holy.

keyTerms.meaning: From bottom to top, listing the vessels from smallest to largest
They became holy, made holy by the vessel of the מקדש
Measure, work out the amounts

phrases.english: According to the one who said from bottom to top,
phrases.notes: This means listing the vessels from smallest to largest.

phrases.english: he holds that the overflow of the measures became holy,
and the Merciful One gave Moshe a quarter,
phrases.notes: A quarter of a הין, the smallest vessel, which he used to build up the bigger amounts.

phrases.english: and said to him: Measure with it,
so that the overflow goes in.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains how the upward order fits רבי יוחנן's answer.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Counting upward means the overflow was poured in and counted, so it is holy.

steps.title: Counting downward: the overflow is not holy
steps.stepSummary: The one who lists the vessels from big to small holds that the overflow is not holy, because משה started with a הין and divided downward, so the overflow fell away.
steps.simpleTranslation: The one who lists from big to small holds that the overflow of the measures did not become holy. הקב"ה gave משה a הין vessel and told him: Measure with this, so the overflow goes out.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן now explains the other side. The one who lists from big to small holds that the overflow is not holy.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here משה started with the biggest vessel, the הין, and poured from it into smaller vessels. The overflow on the outside of the big vessel does not go into the smaller one. It falls away, so it was never part of the measure and is not holy.

keyTerms.meaning: From top to bottom, listing the vessels from largest to smallest
The largest measuring vessel in the list

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי יוחנן, counting upward (from the רביעית) means the overflow is holy. Counting downward (from the הין) means it is not.

phrases.english: According to the one who said from top to bottom,
he holds that the overflow of the measures did not become holy,
and the Merciful One gave Moshe a hin,
and said to him: Measure with this,
so that the overflow goes out.
phrases.notes: When you pour from the big vessel into a smaller one, the drips on the outside fall away and are not counted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The mirror image of step 8, giving the downward view.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Counting downward means the overflow fell away and was not counted, so it is not holy.

steps.title: אביי: the argument is about the word "full"
steps.stepSummary: אביי says the overflow question does not depend on the order of the list. Either side could hold either way. The real argument is about the meaning of מלאים.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: According to everyone, about the overflow of the measures you could say it became holy, and you could say it did not. Here they argue about "full."
steps.whatsHappening: אביי gives a different answer to the question in step 6. He says the order of the list has nothing to do with the overflow, and points instead to the word מלאים. This sets up the explanation that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן had tied each order to one view on overflow. אביי breaks that link: both רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה could hold either view about overflow. He moves the argument to how to understand the word "full."

keyTerms.meaning: According to everyone, both sides agree
One could say, this view is possible
Full

steps.confusionAlert: אביי is not saying the overflow is or is not holy. He is saying that this question is not what רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה are arguing about.

phrases.english: Abaye said:
According to everyone, the overflow of the measures,
one could say they became holy,
and one could say they did not become holy,
and here they argue about "full."
phrases.notes: This is the word "full" in the פסוק about the נשיאים' offerings (במדבר 7:13).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different answer to step 6's question than רבי יוחנן's answer in steps 7-9.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The disagreement is not about overflow but about the meaning of the word "full."

steps.title: Big-to-small means exactly full
steps.stepSummary: אביי explains that the one who lists the vessels from big to small holds that 'מלאים' means exact: not less and not more.
steps.simpleTranslation: The one who listed the vessels from the biggest down to the smallest holds that 'full' means exact. The vessel may hold no less and no more than its set amount.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי gives the first half of his explanation. The big-to-small order comes from reading 'מלאים' as 'exactly full.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: If you start with the biggest vessel and split its liquid into smaller ones, each measure comes out exact. So the person who lists from big to small holds that the measure must be precise, with nothing extra and nothing missing.

keyTerms.meaning: Full. The word whose meaning is being debated.
From top to bottom: listing from the biggest vessel to the smallest.
That it should not be less and should not be more. In other words, exact.

phrases.english: The one who said from top to bottom,
holds that 'full' means
that it should not be less and should not be more.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Fills in the first side of אביי's claim that the argument is about the meaning of מלאים.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Big-to-small order reflects reading מלאים as an exact measure.

steps.title: Small-to-big means at least full
steps.stepSummary: The one who lists from small to big holds that 'מלאים' only means not less. A little extra still counts as full.
steps.simpleTranslation: The one who listed the vessels from the smallest up to the biggest holds that 'full' means it must not hold less. If it holds a bit more, we still call it 'full.'
steps.whatsHappening: אביי gives the second half of his explanation, the view behind the small-to-big order.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If you build up the bigger measures from the small one, a little extra slips in each time you pour. This side does not mind, because to them 'full' means at least the amount, and some extra is fine.

keyTerms.meaning: From bottom to top: listing from the smallest vessel to the biggest.
It holds extra, more than the set amount.
I can still call it this. The name still fits.

steps.whatToRemember: According to אביי, both orders of the list come from one question: does 'מלאים' mean exactly full, or at least full?

phrases.english: And the one who said from bottom to top,
'full' means that it should not be less,
but if it holds more,
I still call it 'full.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes אביי's contrast by giving the opposite reading of מלאים.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Small-to-big order reflects reading מלאים as a minimum: extra is allowed.

steps.title: רבי שמעון's point that there was no הין vessel makes sense
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes רבי שמעון, who says there was no הין vessel in the מקדש, and says his argument against the רבנן is a good one.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was said: רבי שמעון says there was no הין vessel there. רבי שמעון is making a good point to the רבנן!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic. It quotes רבי שמעון and backs him, which puts pressure on the רבנן to explain why a הין vessel would exist.
steps.deeperAnalysis: No offering in the מקדש ever needed a full הין of liquid. So why keep a measuring cup that size? Saying 'he spoke well' turns רבי שמעון's view into a challenge that the רבנן now have to answer.

keyTerms.meaning: A large liquid measure, the biggest vessel on the list.
He is speaking well; he has a good point.

phrases.english: The Master said:

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר לֹא הָיָה שָׁם הִין,
phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon says there was no hin there,

phrases.aramaic: שַׁפִּיר קָאָמַר לְהוּ רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן לְרַבָּנַן!
phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon is saying well to the Rabbis!

steps.triggerLanguage: שַׁפִּיר קָאָמַר לְהוּ רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן לְרַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the order-of-vessels question and opens a new one: did a הין vessel exist at all?
steps.kashyaTarget: The רבנן's view that there was a הין measuring vessel in the מקדש.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: No offering uses a full הין, so a vessel that size would have no purpose.

steps.title: The רבנן: משה made a הין for the anointing oil
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן answer that there was a הין vessel, because משה made one to measure the שמן המשחה, as the פסוק says.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the רבנן? There was a הין that משה made for the anointing oil, as it is written: 'and of olive oil a הין.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the רבנן's answer to רבי שמעון's challenge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The הין vessel did have a use, just not for regular offerings. משה needed it once, to measure the oil for the שמן המשחה, and the פסוק says that oil came to exactly one הין.

keyTerms.meaning: The special anointing oil made by משה.
Olive oil.

phrases.english: And the Rabbis? There was a hin
that Moses made for the anointing oil,
as it is written: 'and of olive oil a hin.'

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבָּנַן – הֲוָה הִין דַּעֲבַד מֹשֶׁה לְשֶׁמֶן הַמִּשְׁחָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 13.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Points to a use from the פסוק that the challenge overlooked.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A הין vessel would be useless, so it could not have existed.
steps.terutzMaskana: It existed because משה made it to measure the שמן המשחה.

steps.title: The root of the argument: was the הין put away or kept?
steps.stepSummary: Both sides agree משה made a הין. רבי שמעון holds it was a one-time vessel that was hidden away. The רבנן hold that once it existed, it stayed.
steps.simpleTranslation: One master holds: since it was not needed for later generations, משה made it only for that time, and then it was hidden away. The other holds: since it existed, it stayed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains exactly where רבי שמעון and the רבנן disagree.
steps.deeperAnalysis: No one argues about whether משה made a הין. The question is what happened to it afterward. רבי שמעון says a vessel needed only once was put away. The רבנן say that once it was made, it stayed in the מקדש, even though it was no longer needed.

keyTerms.meaning: For future generations; permanent.
For that time only; temporary.
It was hidden away, put out of use.
Since it existed, it stayed.

steps.whatToRemember: רבי שמעון and the רבנן agree that משה made a הין. They argue only about whether a one-time vessel was put away or kept.
steps.confusionAlert: רבי שמעון does not deny that משה ever made a הין. He only says it was not kept in the מקדש later on.

phrases.english: One master holds:
since it was not needed for future generations,
he made it only for that time, and it was hidden away,
and the other holds: since it existed, it remained.

steps.triggerLanguage: מָר סָבַר: כֵּיוָן דִּלְדוֹרוֹת לָא הֲוָה צְרִיךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the רבנן's answer, shows that both sides agree on the facts and differ on what happened to the vessel later.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The argument comes down to whether a vessel made for a one-time need was put away (רבי שמעון) or stayed in the מקדש (רבנן).

steps.title: Why must רבי שמעון replace the missing הין?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רבי שמעון needs a seventh vessel at all, once he says there was no הין.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Master said: 'Which vessel shall I bring in its place?' Why must he include another one? Couldn't he just not count one?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes רבי שמעון from the ברייתא and asks why he bothers to find a replacement for the הין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון said there was no הין vessel, so he added a different vessel to keep the list at seven. The גמרא asks why the number seven matters at all. Why not just list six?

keyTerms.meaning: I will bring in its place, a replacement
Is it not possible? Can't one manage without?
to bring in, to include in the count
A large liquid measure, the vessel רבי שמעון says was not in the מקדש

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר מָר: וְאֶת מִי אָבִיא תַּחְתָּיו.
phrases.english: The Master said: 'And which one shall I bring in its place?'
Is it not possible to not include one?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to a detail in רבי שמעון's words from the ברייתא discussed in steps 13-15.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי שמעון's need to name a replacement vessel for the הין.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the הין did not exist, nothing seems to force him to keep the count at seven.

steps.title: There is a tradition of seven liquid measures
steps.stepSummary: Like the tradition of two סמיכות in communal offerings, there was a tradition that the מקדש had seven liquid measures.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רבינא said: there is a tradition that there are two cases of סמיכה on communal offerings. Here too there is a tradition that there were seven liquid measures in the מקדש.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the number seven is a fixed tradition, so רבי שמעון must fill the seventh spot.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא compares this to another case where a number is known by tradition: two communal offerings that get סמיכה. Since 'seven liquid measures' is a set number from tradition, removing the הין forces him to name a different seventh vessel.

keyTerms.meaning: It is learned by tradition (handed down, not learned from a פסוק)
Leaning one's hands on the head of an offering
The community, communal offerings
Measuring vessels for liquids

steps.whatToRemember: The count of seven liquid measures in the מקדש is a fixed tradition. That is why רבי שמעון had to replace the הין with another vessel.

phrases.english: As רבינא said:
It is learned by tradition that there are two cases of placing hands on communal offerings,
here too it is learned by tradition

phrases.aramaic: דְּשֶׁבַע מִדּוֹת שֶׁל לַח הָיוּ בְּמִקְדָּשׁ.
phrases.english: that there were seven measures for liquids in the Temple.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 16.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Appeal to a received tradition of a fixed number
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The number seven is just a description and could change.
steps.terutzMaskana: Seven is a tradition, so a replacement is needed.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר ברבי צדוק: the הין had markings
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's view of רבי אלעזר ברבי צדוק that markings on the הין measured the different amounts.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר ברבי צדוק says: there were markings on the הין.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the view of רבי אלעזר ברבי צדוק from the משנה to set up a question about it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He holds that one הין vessel had lines marking the smaller amounts for the different offerings. If so, separate vessels were not needed. This seems to clash with the tradition of seven measures.

keyTerms.meaning: Marked lines or notches showing measurement levels

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar, son of Rabbi Tzadok, says:
There were markings on the hin.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a view from the משנה that seems to conflict with the tradition just stated.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A single הין vessel with markings served for the various measures.

steps.title: Doesn't he accept the seven measures?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether רבי אלעזר ברבי צדוק does not accept the tradition of seven measures.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does he not hold of the seven measures?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי אלעזר ברבי צדוק using the tradition from step 17.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If one marked הין covers all the amounts, there seem to be no seven separate vessels. That appears to go against the tradition of seven liquid measures.

keyTerms.meaning: He does not hold of it, he does not accept it

phrases.english: And does he not hold of the seven measures?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the view quoted in step 18 using the tradition from step 17.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אלעזר ברבי צדוק's marked הין.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: One marked vessel replaces several vessels, which goes against the tradition of seven measures.

steps.title: First answer: he does not accept the tradition
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא simply says that רבי אלעזר ברבי צדוק does not hold of the tradition of seven measures.
steps.simpleTranslation: He does not hold of it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא's first answer: yes, he does not accept the tradition of seven measures.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Instead of resolving the clash, the גמרא accepts it. The tradition from step 17 is not shared by everyone, and רבי אלעזר ברבי צדוק is one who disagrees.

phrases.english: He does not hold of it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 19 by admitting the disagreement.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Everyone accepts the tradition of seven measures.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי אלעזר ברבי צדוק does not accept it.

steps.title: Second answer: seven ways of measuring
steps.stepSummary: Or, he accepts the tradition but reads it as seven amounts to measure, not seven separate vessels.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or if you want, say: what does 'seven measures' mean? Seven measurements.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second answer: רבי אלעזר ברבי צדוק does accept the tradition, but he understands it differently.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Seven measures' can mean seven set amounts, not seven physical vessels. A marked הין can give all seven amounts, so his view fits the tradition.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you want, say instead (introduces another answer)
Acts or amounts of measuring
Measures, here read as measuring vessels or as amounts

steps.whatToRemember: There are two ways to explain רבי אלעזר ברבי צדוק. Either he rejects the tradition of seven measures, or he reads 'seven measures' as seven amounts that the marked הין could give.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up מִדּוֹת (measures or vessels) with מְדִידוֹת (measurings). The second answer depends on this small difference in wording.

phrases.english: And if you want, say:
What is meant by 'seven measures'?
Seven measurings.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a second answer to step 19, different from step 20.
steps.terutzMaskana: It means seven amounts, which one marked vessel can provide.

steps.title: New משנה: what the רביעית was used for
steps.stepSummary: The משנה explains that the רביעית measured water for the מצורע and oil for the נזיר.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: What was the רביעית used for? A רביעית of water for the מצורע, and a רביעית of oil for the נזיר.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It goes through the measuring vessels and says what each one was used for, starting with the רביעית.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה ties each measuring vessel to a real use in the מקדש. The רביעית served for water in the purifying of a מצורע and for oil in the loaves a נזיר brings.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה, the opening of a new משנה
A quarter of a לוג
A person with צרעת who goes through a purifying process
A person who took a vow of נזירות and brings offerings at the end

phrases.english: MISHNA:
What was the quarter-log used for?
A quarter-log of water for the leper,
and a quarter-log of oil for the nazirite.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה about the uses of each measure.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The רביעית measured water for the מצורע and oil for the נזיר.

steps.title: What the חצי לוג was used for
steps.stepSummary: The משנה continues: the חצי לוג measured water for the סוטה and oil for the תודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: What was the חצי לוג used for? A חצי לוג of water for the סוטה, and a חצי לוג of oil for the תודה.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה continues its list and explains the use of the חצי לוג.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה keeps the same pattern: each measure had one use for water and one for oil. The חצי לוג served for the water given to the סוטה and for the oil in the breads of the תודה.

keyTerms.meaning: Half of a לוג
A woman suspected of adultery who goes through the bitter-water process
The thanks offering, brought with loaves

phrases.english: What was the half-log used for?
A half-log of water for the sota,
and a half-log of oil for the thanks offering.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה's list from step 22.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The חצי לוג measured water for the סוטה and oil for the תודה.

steps.title: The לוג vessel measured oil for all מנחות
steps.stepSummary: The משנה continues its list of vessels: the לוג vessel measured oil for every מנחה.
steps.simpleTranslation: With the one-לוג vessel, they measured the oil for all the meal offerings.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה is still listing the measuring vessels and what each one was used for. Now it reaches the לוג, which measured oil for the מנחות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The רביעית and the חצי לוג were each used for specific offerings. The לוג is broader, because it served all the regular מנחות. This sets up the next question: what happens with a very large מנחה?

keyTerms.meaning: A liquid measure, one of the vessels in the מקדש
Meal offerings made of flour, usually mixed with oil
Measures

phrases.english: And with the log one would measure
for all the meal offerings.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה's list of measuring vessels after the רביעית and the חצי לוג.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The לוג vessel measured the oil for all standard מנחות.

steps.title: A מנחה of sixty עשרונים gets sixty לוג of oil
steps.stepSummary: The תנא קמא says the oil grows with the flour, so a מנחה of sixty עשרונים needs sixty לוג of oil.
steps.simpleTranslation: Even a מנחה of sixty עשרונים of flour gets sixty לוג of oil.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives the first opinion, the תנא קמא, about a very large מנחה. Each עשרון of flour gets its own לוג of oil.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The idea is a fixed ratio: one עשרון of flour needs one לוג of oil. So the amount of oil rises together with the amount of flour, even up to sixty.

keyTerms.meaning: A tenth of an איפה, the basic unit of flour for a מנחה
Sixty
The first, unnamed opinion in a משנה

phrases.english: Even a meal offering of sixty tenths,
one gives it sixty log.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains how the לוג is used when a מנחה is very large.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Each עשרון of flour needs one לוג of oil, so sixty עשרונים need sixty לוג.
steps.triggerLanguage: אֲפִילּוּ מִנְחָה שֶׁל שִׁשִּׁים עִשָּׂרוֹן, נוֹתֵן לָהּ שִׁשִּׁים לוֹג

steps.title: רבי אליעזר בן יעקב: every מנחה gets just one לוג
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר בן יעקב argues that any מנחה, no matter how large, gets only one לוג of oil, and he learns it from a פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אליעזר בן יעקב says: even a מנחה of sixty עשרונים has only its one לוג, as it says, "for a meal offering, and a לוג of oil."
steps.whatsHappening: A second opinion disagrees with the תנא קמא. For רבי אליעזר בן יעקב, the oil stays at one לוג per מנחה, no matter how much flour there is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק places the words "מנחה" and "לוג שמן" next to each other. He reads that as one לוג for each מנחה, not one לוג for each עשרון. So the argument is about the unit: does the oil follow the offering or the flour?

keyTerms.meaning: Its own single לוג
It has only
As it says (introduces a פסוק)

steps.confusionAlert: Both opinions agree that a regular one-עשרון מנחה gets one לוג. They argue only about a מנחה that has more than one עשרון.

phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer ben Yaakov says:
Even a meal offering of sixty tenths
has only its log,
as it is stated: "for a meal offering, and a log of oil."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with the תנא קמא's ratio of one לוג for each עשרון.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Any מנחה gets exactly one לוג of oil, whatever its size.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up two models: oil measured by the amount of flour, or oil measured per offering.

steps.title: The oil amounts for a bull, a ram, and a lamb
steps.stepSummary: The משנה lists the לוגים needed for the offerings that come with each animal: six for a bull, four for a ram, three for a lamb.
steps.simpleTranslation: Six לוגים for a bull, four for a ram, and three for a lamb.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה now moves to the מנחות and נסכים that are brought along with animal קרבנות. It gives the number of לוגים for each kind of animal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These numbers match the תורה's measures in הין: a half הין, a third, and a quarter. One הין is twelve לוגים. A bigger animal gets more.

keyTerms.meaning: Bull
Ram
Lamb
A larger measure equal to twelve לוגים

phrases.english: Six for a bull, and four for a ram,
phrases.notes: "Six" means six לוגים, which is half a הין. Four is a third of a הין.

phrases.english: and three for a lamb.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from standalone מנחות to the oil that accompanies animal offerings.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A bull gets 6 לוגים, a ram 4, and a lamb 3.
steps.triggerLanguage: שִׁשָּׁה לַפָּר, וְאַרְבָּעָה לָאַיִל, וּשְׁלֹשָׁה לַכֶּבֶשׂ

steps.title: Three and a half לוגים of oil for the מנורה
steps.stepSummary: The מנורה needs three and a half לוגים of oil, which is half a לוג for each of its seven lamps.
steps.simpleTranslation: Three and a half לוגים for the מנורה, half a לוג for each lamp.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה ends this list with the oil needed for the מנורה each day.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The מנורה has seven lamps. At half a לוג each, the total comes to three and a half לוגים. The amount per lamp matches the size of the חצי לוג vessel, though the משנה did not list the מנורה among that vessel's uses.

keyTerms.meaning: The seven-branched lamp in the מקדש
Lamp
And a half

steps.whatToRemember: The לוג measured oil for the מנחות, with an argument over large מנחות. Animal offerings get 6, 4, or 3 לוגים, and the מנורה gets half a לוג for each of its seven lamps.

phrases.english: Three and a half for the Candelabrum,
half a log for each lamp.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds the last item to the משנה's list of oil amounts.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The מנורה receives 3½ לוגים of oil, half a לוג per lamp.
steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁלֹשָׁה וּמֶחֱצָה לַמְּנוֹרָה, חֲצִי לוֹג לְכׇל נֵר

steps.title: רבי asks why the רביעית vessel was anointed
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins with רבי puzzling over the purpose of the רביעית vessel. He starts checking the first possible use, the purification of a מצורע.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: רבי was sitting and had a difficulty: why was the רביעית vessel anointed? If you say it was for the מצורע...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens by asking what the רביעית measuring vessel was actually used for, since it was anointed as a holy vessel. It is setting up a search: it starts testing the מצורע as one possible answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Anointing a vessel made it a כלי שרת, a holy vessel for the עבודה, so it needed a real use in the בית המקדש. רבי could not find one for the רביעית, so he goes option by option. The first option is the מצורע, and the words אִי מְצוֹרָע begin a test of that idea, which continues in the next lines.

keyTerms.meaning: The discussion that explains and analyzes the משנה
He had a difficulty. Something was bothering him and did not make sense yet
A quarter of a לוג. Here it means the measuring vessel of that size
Was anointed with the anointing oil, which made the vessel holy
A person with צרעת who goes through a purification process

steps.confusionAlert: Don't read רבי's question as doubting that the רביעית existed or was holy. He accepts both. He only wants to know what it was needed for.

phrases.english: GEMARA:
Rabbi was sitting and had a difficulty:
phrases.notes: This רבי is רבי יהודה הנשיא.

phrases.english: Why was the quarter-log vessel anointed?
If you say it was for the leper,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the גמרא's analysis of the משנה's list of measuring vessels, focusing on the smallest one, the רביעית.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What purpose in the בית המקדש required the רביעית vessel to be anointed as a holy vessel?
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's statement that the anointed רביעית vessel was used for the מצורע and the נזיר.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A vessel anointed as a holy vessel must have a use that needs holiness. רבי checks each listed use, starting with the מצורע, to see whether it really requires one.
